Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these four appeared first?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Max Born is a physicist. During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Antoine Lavoisier is a chemist. It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
What is the atomic number of Oxygen?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
In what year was Werner Heisenberg born?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Glutathione discovered?
Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
In what year was Morphine discovered?
Morphine, formerly known as morphium, is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Acetylcysteine: Pfizer. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Radon?
Radon: Friedrich Ernst Dorn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Who is credited with discovering Tautavel Man?
Tautavel Man: Henry de Lumley. Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans which—from approximately 550,000 to 400,000 years ago—inhabited the Caune de l’Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Who is credited with discovering MDMA?
MDMA: Anton Köllisch. MDMA was first synthesized in 1912 by Merck chemist Anton Köllisch.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.

Found mainly in New Guinea, which family of forty-four species — the males famous for extravagant, elaborate plumage sprouting from their beaks, wings, tails, or heads — is confined largely to dense rainforest?
Bird-of-paradise are members of the family Paradisaeidae of the order Passeriformes.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.
Director of Columbia's Center for Sustainable Development, which economist led the United Nations Millennium Project's work on the Millennium Development Goals?
Jeffrey Sachs (SAKS; born November 5, 1954) is an American economist and public policy analyst.
Native to Central and South American rainforests, this frugivorous nocturnal mammal related to raccoons and coatis shares its 'honey bear' nickname with an unrelated species — which animal?
Kinkajou (/kkdu/; Potos flavus) is a mammal of the family Procyonidae, a relative to olingos, coatis, raccoons, and the ringtail and cacomistle.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
This German-British theoretical physicist won a Nobel Prize for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. Who is he?
Max Born (11 December 1882 - 5 January 1970) was a German-British theoretical physicist who was instrumental in the development of quantum mechanics.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.

Native only to New Zealand and resembling a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that was hugely diverse in the Mesozoic era, with fossils dating to the Middle Triassic — what's the animal?
Tuatara (Mori:; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.

Native to freshwater and brackish habitats across western Eurasia, this ray-finned fish in the perch family, related to perch, ruffe, and darters, has become a popular game species well beyond its original range. Name it?
Zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Marked by inadequate cortisol and aldosterone production in the adrenal glands, this rare, long-term endocrine disorder is also known as primary adrenal insufficiency — what is it?
Addison's disease: Endocrine disorder. Addison's disease arises when the adrenal gland does not produce sufficient amounts of the steroid hormones cortisol and (sometimes) aldosterone.
His mother and wife were both deaf, which steered this Scottish-born inventor toward hearing devices — and, in 1876, the first U.S. patent for the telephone. Who was he?
Alexander Graham Bell: Inventor of the telephone (1847–1922)

These coiled-shelled cephalopods, more closely related to octopuses than to nautiluses despite the resemblance, thrived from the Devonian until vanishing around the dinosaur extinction 66 million years ago — what are they?
Ammonoidea: Extinct subclass of cephalopod molluscs.

Their larvae — nicknamed "doodlebugs" in North America for the marks they leave — dig sandy pits to trap passing ants, while the dusk-flying adults are often mistaken for dragonflies. What insect is this?
This American psychiatrist and pharmaceutical marketer amassed the world's largest personal collection of Chinese art, later donated to the Smithsonian — who is he?
Arthur M. Sackler: American physician and executive (1913–1987)

Among the first life forms on Earth and typically just a few micrometres long, these single-celled prokaryotes thrive everywhere from hot springs to radioactive waste and drive the putrefaction stage of decay — what are they?
A red supergiant in Orion so vast that, placed at the Sun's position, it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, this variable star is designated Alpha Orionis — which star?
Betelgeuse: Red supergiant star in the constellation Orion. It is usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky and, after Rigel, the second brightest in its constellation.
After scrapping its Sonic Cruiser idea, this American planemaker launched an efficiency-focused wide-body in 2004 with a first order from All Nippon Airways — which aircraft?

Native to Europe, West Asia, and parts of North Africa, this widely introduced game fish is one of the world's worst invasive species outside its home range, with regional names like sewin in Wales and finnock in Scotland — which species is it?
Brown trout: Species of fish. Brown trout are highly adaptable and have evolved numerous ecotypes/subspecies.

Roughly a third of deaths from this group of over 100 diseases trace to tobacco, alcohol, obesity, poor diet and inactivity, and its malignant tumors are defined by uncontrolled cell growth that can spread — what is it?

Cancer: Group of diseases involving cell growth. Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.

This branch of metabolism breaks down large molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids into smaller units, releasing energy as cells convert the leftovers into waste like carbon dioxide and urea — what's it called?
Catabolism: Set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units.
Built after a 1962 tech-transfer deal with the Soviets fell short on documentation, this Chinese fighter jet is a reverse-engineered derivative of the MiG-21 — which aircraft?
Chengdu J-7: Chinese version of the Soviet MiG-21.
This lincosamide antibiotic treats infections from strep throat to acne, but raises the risk of a specific gut infection roughly fourfold — what is it?
Clindamycin: Antibiotic. It can also be used to treat acne, and some cases of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
Its species name honors Colchis, an ancient region on the Black Sea, and it's often released into the wild as a game bird — which Asian-native, ring-necked bird is this?
Common pheasant: Species of bird. The common pheasant (Phasianus colchicus), ring-necked pheasant, or blue-headed pheasant, is a bird in the pheasant family (Phasianidae).
First described in 1963, this rare disorder from a partial deletion on chromosome 5 gets its French name from the distinctive feline-sounding cry of affected infants — what is it called?
Cri du chat syndrome: Human medical condition.
At just 37 this American biologist won a 1975 Nobel for discovering reverse transcriptase, later running Caltech and founding the Whitehead Institute — who is he?
David Baltimore: American biologist and Nobel laureate (1938–2025)
These warmblooded reptiles ruled the land for the whole Mesozoic, and one feathered lineage of theirs survived the extinction 66 million years ago as today's birds — what group is this?
Dinosaur: Clade of reptiles. Since then, mounted fossil dinosaur skeletons have been major attractions at museums worldwide, and dinosaurs have become an enduring part of popular culture.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.
Occurring in the cytosol, this ten-step metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate while generating ATP and NADH — what process is it?
Glycolysis: Series of interconnected biochemical reactions.
A founder of psychophysics, this German scientist captured how sensation relates to stimulus in a logarithmic law that now bears his and Weber's names — who was he?
Gustav Fechner: German experimental psychologist, physicist, and philosopher (1801–1887)
This Dutch-born entrepreneur produced Japan's first major turn-based role-playing game and later secured the console distribution rights to a Russian puzzle game called Tetris — who is he?
Henk Rogers: Dutch-born American computer programmer (born 1953)
Despite the name, this 'living fossil' is no crustacean at all — it's a chelicerate, kin to spiders and scorpions, and its three-part body ends in a spiky tail called a telson. What creature is it?
Horseshoe crab: Family of basal chelicerates.
This physical phenomenon describes how a system's current state depends on its past history, forming looping curves in magnets and giving hard disk drives their memory — what is it?
Hysteresis: Dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

He won the 1944 Nobel Prize for his resonance method of recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei, and was among the first Americans to work on the cavity magnetron behind radar and microwave ovens — which physicist?
This German craftsman's mechanical printing press — with its oil-based ink and adjustable metal type — sparked an information revolution that helped fuel the Renaissance and Reformation — who is he?
Johannes Gutenberg: German inventor and craftsman (c. 1393–1406 – 1468)
Named from a Tongan and Marquesan word meaning 'bitter,' this pepper-family plant's ground root becomes a ceremonial Pacific Islands drink that numbs the mouth — what is it?
Kava: Species of plant. Kava or kava kava (Piper methysticum: Latin 'pepper' and Latinized Greek 'intoxicating') is a plant in the pepper family, native to the Pacific Islands.
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Also known as the deer ked, this blood-sucking fly sheds its own wings once it lands on a host and burrows through the fur to feed — what species is it?
Lipoptena cervi: Species of fly. Lipoptena cervi, the deer ked or deer fly, is a species of biting fly in the family of louse flies, Hippoboscidae.
Often a complication of cancer treatment, this incurable, progressive swelling condition is managed with compression therapy and manual drainage rather than diuretics — what is it?
Lymphedema: Swelling due to a compromised lymphatic system.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Comprising 18 to 24 species that hybridize freely where their ranges overlap, this genus of the mint family thrives in wet, moist soils worldwide — what is it?
Mentha: Genus of flowering plants in the family Lamiaceae.
Soviet pilots nicknamed this 1972 gunship the 'flying tank,' a helicopter NATO calls 'Hind' that can also haul eight troops and still flies in 52 countries. What is it?
Mil Mi-24: Family of assault and attack helicopters.
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.

Flown by William J. Knight to a record 4,520 mph in 1967 — a mark that still stands — this rocket-powered aircraft was part of an experimental series operated by the Air Force and NASA — which aircraft?
North American X-15: Rocket-powered aircraft and spaceplane operated by the US Air Force and NASA.
Mostly black on top, white below, and sporting unmistakable white eye patches, this cosmopolitan apex predator is actually the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family. What is it?
Orca: Largest living species of dolphin.
Secreted by small neck glands when blood calcium runs low, this peptide messenger raises calcium levels and boosts active vitamin D production — which one?
Parathyroid hormone: Mammalian protein found in humans.
In mathematics, what term describes both an ordered arrangement of a set's members and the act of rearranging them, as seen in the six possible orderings of three distinct numbers?
Permutation: Mathematical version of an order change.
Evergreen conifers of the genus Pinus, these trees grow their needle leaves in bunches of two to five and yield both the nuts used in pesto and the resin that flavors retsina wine?
Pine: Genus of coniferous trees. A pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.
Better known in the kitchen as cream of tartar, this winemaking byproduct helps stabilize egg whites for fluffier meringues — what compound is it?
Potassium bitartrate: Chemical salt used in cooking as cream of tartar.

Marked by delusions, hallucinations and disorganized thinking, this state — not a diagnosis itself — often stems from schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or alcohol-related brain damage — what is it called?
Psychosis: Abnormal condition of the mind.
Also called broccoli rabe, this bitter, vitamin K-rich cruciferous vegetable is a Mediterranean cuisine staple with edible leaves, buds, and stems — what is it?
This blue supergiant in Orion, also known as Beta Orionis, outshines the Sun by up to 363,000 times and anchors a system of at least four stars — which star?
Rigel: Brightest star in the constellation Orion.
A Stanford physicist who joined NASA in 1978, she became the first American woman in space in 1983 — and, at 32, the youngest American to fly there. Who is she?
Sally Ride: American physicist and astronaut (1951–2012)
This class of central nervous system depressant increases GABA activity to calm irritability and anxiety, distinct from drugs used mainly to induce sleep — what is it?
Sedative: Drug that reduces excitement without inducing sleep.
This structural framework supporting an animal's body can take the form of a rigid outer shell, an internal bony frame, or simply fluid pressure inside the body. What is it?
Skeleton: Part of the body that forms the supporting structure.

First described in 1915 by a German paleontologist from Egyptian fossils that were destroyed during World War II, this dinosaur genus wasn't represented by new material until the early 2000s — which genus?
Spinosaurus: Genus of spinosaurid dinosaur. The genus was known first from Egyptian remains discovered in 1912 and described by German palaeontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915.
The first variable-sweep-wing aircraft to enter Soviet service, this fighter-bomber was produced from 1967 to 1990 and exported in variants flown across the Arab world — which jet?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
The lone living family within its primate infraorder, these small Southeast Asian mammals favor forests thick with liana vines, which give them vertical support as they climb — which animal?
In tetrapods this body region between the neck and abdomen houses the heart, lungs, and thymus gland, while in insects and crustaceans it forms one of three main body segments — what is it called?
Thorax: Frontal part of an animal's body, between its head and abdomen.
Usually caused by a new genetic mutation rather than inherited, which disorder produces deformities of the ears, eyes, cheekbones, and chin but typically leaves intelligence normal?
Treacher Collins syndrome: Human genetic disorder. The degree to which a person is affected may vary from mild to severe.
A breakdown product of purine nucleotides found naturally in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can trigger gout and kidney stones — what is it?
Uric acid: Organic compound. Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
Belonging to the same family as kangaroos but generally smaller, this Australian marsupial has also been introduced to New Zealand, Hawaii, and the UK — what is it?
Wallaby: Macropods of Australia and New Guinea.
With atomic number 54, this dense, colorless noble gas was the first to form a stable chemical compound, and now doubles as a general anesthetic and ion-thruster propellant — which element?
Xenon: Chemical element with atomic number 54 (Xe). It is a dense, colorless, odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts.
The symbol for curium is Cm. Curium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cm and atomic number 96.
What is the chemical symbol for uranium?
The symbol for uranium is U. Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.

River Phoenix: River Jude Phoenix (né Bottom; August 23, 1970 – October 31, 1993) was an American actor and musician.
In what year was Deepika Padukone born?
Deepika Padukone: Deepika Prakash Padukone (pronounced [d̪iːpɪkaː pəɖʊkoːɳeː]; born 5 January 1986) is an Indian actress who works predominantly in Hindi films.
In what year was Jennifer Love Hewitt born?
Jennifer Love Hewitt (born February 21, 1979) is an American actress, singer, producer and director.
In what year was Emily Blunt born?
Emily Blunt: Emily Olivia Laura Blunt (born 23 February 1983) is a British actress.
In what year was Saoirse Ronan born?
Saoirse Ronan: Saoirse Una Ronan ( SUR-shə OO-nə ROH-nən; born 12 April 1994) is an American-born Irish actress.
In what year was Rowan Atkinson born?
Rowan Atkinson: Rowan Sebastian Atkinson (born 6 January 1955) is an English actor, comedian, and writer.
In what year was James Spader born?
James Spader: James Todd Spader ( SPAY-dər; born February 7, 1960) is an American actor.

Julian Assange: Julian Paul Assange (ə-SAHNZH; né Hawkins; born 3 July 1971) is an Australian editor, programmer, and publisher who founded WikiLeaks in 2006.
In what year was Reese Witherspoon born?
Reese Witherspoon: Laura Jeanne Reese Witherspoon (born March 22, 1976) is an American actress and producer.

Emily Ratajkowski: Emily O'Hara Ratajkowski ( RAT-ə-KOW-skee, Polish: [ratajˈkɔfskʲi]; born June 7, 1991), known occasionally as EmRata, is an American model and actress.
